items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: It was on account of Jack Wiggins, John Bowles, you know, Buckin' Bowles, and Walter Beatty and people like that, Mills, Buddy Bradley, Florence Meers, you know.

ctx.x: the words to a song that I knew my mother liked, which was "Harvest Moon" and "Carolina Moon" and "Darktown Strutter's Ball." So those were the three songs that she taught me the words to, how to say them, sing them, you know. And I went in -- when I went in to the show, the amateur contest, the people liked my singing, and all, you know, and they were saying, more, more, come back, more, dance, dance.

Now, I didn't have those bottle tops on my feet this time, you see, on the stage, but I was barefooted, see. The people wanted to laugh, you see, and I didn't think really that I could dance, you know. I was just learning these steps, you see. So a fellow was standing in the wings offstage, and as I went off the stage and people was applauding and saying, more, more, dance, dance, you know, because they loved dancing in the South, you see, it was very popular. That was on account of Jack Wiggins, John Bowles, you…

And this fellow was standing offstage, and I knew who he was. They say he was Shelton Brooks, you know. So I didn't know his name at that time, and I asked him, I say, "Mister, I says -- what should I do?"
